howThisWorks.title: How a leveraged position works
howThisWorks.intro: Six things decide whether you keep your money on this screen. Each one below says what it does, then what it costs you when the market goes the other way.

leverage.title: Leverage
leverage.body: Leverage multiplies your position, not your money. At 2x, $500 of your own funds controls $1,000 of BTC, so every 1% the price moves changes your balance by 2%.
leverage.risk: Losses multiply by exactly the same amount. At 2x a 50% fall against you wipes out your entire margin; at 10x it only takes 10%.

margin.title: Margin
margin.body: Margin is the money you put up and the most you can lose on the position. It is held aside while the position is open and released when you close it.
margin.risk: It is not a deposit you get back automatically. Losses are taken out of it, and a position closed at a loss returns less than you put in.

liquidation.title: Liquidation price
liquidation.body: The price at which your margin is exhausted and the venue closes the position for you, whether or not you are watching. The ticket shows this figure in red before you commit.
liquidation.risk: There is nothing left afterwards. The margin is gone, the position is closed at whatever the market was doing, and a later recovery in the price does not bring it back.

bracket.title: Take profit and stop loss
bracket.body: Two exit prices you set in advance. The take profit closes you out in profit; the stop closes you out before a loss gets larger. You can attach both when you open, or to a position you already hold.
bracket.risk: Both are triggers, not guaranteed prices. When the market touches your level the position is closed at market, so a fast move can fill you meaningfully worse than the number you set.

cover.title: Cover
cover.body: Cover is insurance on the position. You choose how large a move it protects against — the slider is continuous, and 1σ, 2σ and 3σ are just common settings. A bigger covered move costs more, because it pays out more often.
cover.risk: Cover pays at its boundary, not before it. A move smaller than the one you covered is a loss you take in full, and the premium is spent either way.

custody.title: Where your money sits
custody.body: FLT holds your balance and places the order for you — there is no wallet to connect and nothing to sign. Your buying power is your balance on FLT's ledger, and it is backed by funds held at our custodian.
custody.risk: A position is open until it is closed. Leaving the platform, closing the tab or losing your connection does not flatten it, and funding and losses continue in your absence.

howThisWorks.worked: A worked example. You put up $500 at 2x on BTC at 77,000, so you control about 0.013 BTC. If BTC reaches 81,000 you are up roughly $67; if it falls to 73,000 you are down roughly $67. Your liquidation sits near 38,700 — a 50% fall — and a stop at 75,000 would cap the loss at about $33 instead.

scanner.footerNote: Prices, volume and liquidity are estimates supplied by a third-party market data provider, not by FLT, and are not the price your trade will execute at. Execution pricing comes from on-chain liquidity at the moment you request a quote.

passiveCash.title: Passive cash
passiveCash.description: Let idle cash work in FLT's market-making, for half the profit. You bear the losses.

portfolio.title: Portfolio
portfolio.description: Your FLT account balance, held by FLT on your behalf. The chain is used only to estimate value.
portfolio.noWalletBody: Link a self-custody wallet to see your balances. FLT reads them from the chain and never holds your assets.
portfolio.someBalancesTitle: Some balances could not be read
portfolio.networkUnreachableOne: The network could not be reached for {count} wallet. Those holdings are missing from this view rather than shown as zero.
portfolio.networkUnreachableMany: The network could not be reached for {count} wallets. Those holdings are missing from this view rather than shown as zero.
portfolio.noBalancesBody: You have no balance yet. Money appears here once a deposit has been confirmed.
portfolio.footerNote: The balance is FLT's record of what it holds for you. Estimated values apply third-party prices and will differ from what a trade actually realises. A dash means the value is unknown, never that it is zero.

referrals.title: Referrals
referrals.description: Share a code. They get a free month, you get {pct}% of what FLT earns from them.

upgrade.title: Upgrade
upgrade.description: What a plan would be worth, as arithmetic rather than a feature list.
upgrade.seeSideBySide: See every plan side by side

checkout.title: Checkout
checkout.description: Pay for your plan with EVC Plus.
checkout.noPlanBody: Pick a plan first and we will bring you back here to pay for it.
checkout.unavailableBody: EVC Plus checkout has not been switched on yet. Nothing you enter here will be charged.
checkout.intro: You will dial a USSD code on your own phone to pay merchant {merchant}. Enter the name and number on the EVC account you are paying from, so we can match your payment.
checkout.payerNameHint: Exactly as it appears on your EVC account.
checkout.payerPhoneHint: The number you will pay from.
checkout.receiptTo: We will contact you at {email} if anything is unclear.
checkout.genericError: Something went wrong. Please try again.
checkout.pendingBody: Your plan starts once we have matched this payment against our EVC statement. You can check back on this page.

remittance.title: Send money
remittance.description: Send stablecoin, and have local money delivered to an EVC Plus number.
remittance.closedBody: Money transfer is not switched on. Nothing you enter here would be sent.
remittance.verifyBody: Sending money to someone else needs a verified identity. This is the one part of FLT where we hold your money for a short time, and we are required to know who you are before we do.
remittance.walletBody: You need a verified wallet to send the stablecoin from.
remittance.recipientNameHint: Exactly as it appears on their EVC account.
remittance.recipientPhoneHint: The number the money is delivered to.
remittance.relationshipHint: We are required to ask who is being paid and why.
remittance.connectWallet: Connect your wallet to sign the transfer.
remittance.genericError: Something went wrong. Please try again.
remittance.manualBody: Your stablecoin is confirmed on-chain straight away, but the local money is paid out by a person. It is not delivered the moment you send. You can follow it below.
remittance.receivedBody: {amount} is being sent to {name}. Your payment is confirmed on-chain; the delivery is done by hand, so it is not instant. This page shows the status.

fltWallet.title: FLT wallet
fltWallet.pitch: A wallet FLT creates for you, so you can trade without installing anything. The key is held by Privy, not by FLT — we can never move your funds without the permission below, and you can withdraw to any address at any time.
fltWallet.createError: Could not create the wallet. Please try again.
fltWallet.fundingNote: This wallet is empty until you send funds to it. Money in your other wallets stays where it is — creating this one moves nothing.
fltWallet.permissionBody: To place trades for you without a pop-up each time, FLT needs your permission to instruct this wallet. It only ever sends the trade you asked for, and you can withdraw it at any time.
fltWallet.grantCta: Allow FLT to trade from this wallet
fltWallet.grantedBody: FLT can place the trades you request from this wallet. Withdrawals always go to an address you choose.
fltWallet.grantError: Could not change the permission. Please try again.
fltWallet.termsChangedBody: The permission you gave was for earlier wording. Please read and accept the current terms to keep trading from this wallet.

withdrawPage.title: Withdraw
withdrawPage.description: Take money out of your FLT account. A request reserves the amount; the transfer is sent from the omnibus and your balance moves when it confirms on-chain.
withdrawPage.destinationHint: The wallet to send to. Check it carefully — a withdrawal cannot be reversed.
withdrawPage.overBalance: That is more than your available balance.
withdrawPage.timingNote: Your balance moves when the transfer confirms on-chain. You can follow it in Activity.
withdrawPage.submitted: Withdrawal requested. It will be sent shortly, and your balance updates when it confirms.
withdrawPage.noAssets: You have nothing to withdraw yet.

deposit.cryptoIntro: Send USDC or USDT on Base to your FLT address below. Your balance is credited once we confirm it on-chain.
deposit.cryptoNoticeTitle: Send only USDC or USDT on Base
deposit.cryptoNotice: Other coins or networks may be lost. Ask support if you are not sure.
deposit.fiatIntro: No bank needed. Pay from any phone with EVC Plus, then tell us what you sent.
deposit.evcStep1: Pay EVC merchant {merchant}. Your phone will show the name FTL-IT on the prompt.
deposit.evcStep2: Then enter the phone number you paid from and the amount below.
deposit.evcPrompt: Your phone prompt says FTL-IT. If it does not, stop and contact support.
deposit.withdrawStep1: Open Withdraw and choose the asset and amount.
deposit.withdrawStep2: Enter the address to send to and confirm. Your balance moves when the transfer confirms.
deposit.title: Add money
deposit.description: Add money with crypto or EVC mobile money.
deposit.needsWalletBody: Your money arrives in your own FLT wallet, so you need one before you send anything.
deposit.unavailableBody: We are not accepting transfers at the moment. Nothing you enter here will be charged.
deposit.intro: Your money is converted to dollars and credited to your FLT balance. It stays yours.
deposit.genericError: Something went wrong. Please try again.
deposit.pendingTitle: Your balance is not there yet
deposit.pendingBody: Put the reference on your transfer so we can match it to you. Once we have seen the money and converted it into your balance, your balance appears here.
deposit.payerNameHint: Exactly as it appears where the money is coming from.
deposit.payerPhoneHint: We match this against our statement to find your payment.
deposit.supportNote: This usually takes 1–3 days. Please be patient, and email support@ftlexchange.com if you have any questions or something looks wrong.
